10 memory B-cell states in healthy pediatric tonsil, with no plasma-cell program behind the source plasmablast label

Workshop example run · 2026-11-07

Note: This report was generated by Genie Code in collaboration with a researcher. Review and edit it carefully before sharing it with others.
Summary. We reanalysed a CELLxGENE human tonsil B-cell dataset (21,595 cells, 7 donors, 13 libraries) from raw counts. Data-driven QC kept 18,213 cells (84.3%). After per-donor highly variable gene selection, Harmony integration on donor and Leiden clustering (resolution 0.8), we found 10 memory B-cell state clusters that recover the authors' subtypes, with 1 high-confidence match(es) (FCRL4+ atypical memory B). The source plasmablast label is not supported by plasma-cell gene expression.

Introduction

This dataset profiles memory B cells and plasmablasts from human tonsil (Human tonsil memory B cells scRNA). The question was whether an independent reanalysis from raw counts recovers the published B-cell states.

The approach was a standard scanpy workflow with thresholds derived from the data and confirmed by the analyst, Harmony batch correction on donor, and marker-based cell-state suggestions compared against the author labels.

Results

Unsupervised clustering resolves 10 B-cell states that track the authors' subtypes

All 10 clusters are B-lineage. 8 clusters have a single dominant author subtype covering at least half of their cells, and FCRL4+ memory B cells (cluster 6, 2,200 cells) are recovered as a distinct population (FCRL4+ (80%) author agreement). Resting, activated, pre-germinal-centre, heat-shock-response and CD21-low states are separated. The labels are assistant suggestions from marker genes and need expert review.

The source plasmablast label is not supported by plasma-cell gene expression

The source cell_type column labels 5,159 QC-passing cells as plasmablasts, concentrated in clusters 3 (1,880) and 5 (1,703). These clusters express immediate-early and activation genes, but the highest cluster mean of XBP1 is 0.36 and of JCHAIN 0.33 (log-normalized), with no cluster showing a plasma-cell program.

Discussion

  • The reanalysis reproduces the published memory B-cell state structure, which supports the robustness of those subtypes to an independent pipeline.
  • The plasmablast label in the curated metadata appears to mark activated memory B cells rather than antibody-secreting cells; it should be checked against the original publication before being used downstream.
  • Heat-shock (clusters 4 and 7) and immediate-early (cluster 3) states may partly reflect tissue dissociation stress rather than in vivo biology.

Limitations

  • Residual donor structure remains after Harmony: donor BCP6 makes up 46%-50% of clusters 1, 6, 9 against 18% of all cells.
  • Cell-state labels are LLM suggestions from marker genes, not reference-based annotation, and have not yet been reviewed by an expert.
  • Mitochondrial genes are absent from the matrix, so the mitochondrial filter relies on the authors' precomputed fraction.
  • Only 197 cells come from the second assay, which is too few to assess assay effects separately from donor.

Methods

Data sources

/Volumes/dbacademy/scrna/raw_h5ad/7970bd6b-f752-47a9-8643-2af16855ec49.h5ad

The h5ad file contains 21,595 cells and 19,744 genes from 7 donors and 13 libraries; 10x 5' v1: 21,398 cells; 10x 3' v2: 197 cells. Raw integer counts were taken from .raw (the main matrix is normalized) and Ensembl IDs were mapped to gene symbols with feature_name. The authors had already filtered cells (minimum 1,001 counts and 501 genes per cell in the file).

Quality control

QC thresholds were set from this dataset's distributions (median plus or minus 3 MAD, percentiles) and confirmed by the analyst: mitochondrial fraction below 10.0%, between 600 and 2500 detected genes, removal of author-flagged doublets (DoubletFinder non-singlet or Scrublet positive), and genes detected in at least 3 cells. The matrix contains 0 MT- genes, so the authors' precomputed percent.mito (x100) was used for the mitochondrial filter. This kept 18,213 of 21,595 cells (84.3%) and 16,076 genes.

Normalization, integration and clustering

Counts were normalized to 10,000 per cell and log1p-transformed. 2,000 highly variable genes were selected per donor (scanpy seurat flavour, batch key donor_id). PCA (50 components, HVGs only) was corrected with Harmony (harmonypy, batch key donor_id, random state 0). A 15-nearest-neighbour graph on the first 30 Harmony components fed UMAP and Leiden clustering (igraph, resolution 0.8, 2 iterations). Marker genes were ranked per cluster with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test on log-normalized values. Donor was chosen as the batch key because assay is nested within donor. Analysis ran on Databricks serverless CPU.
